title: Energy, Waves, and Optics - Practice Exam
instructions: Answer all questions. Multiple-choice questions have four options (A, B, C, D). Show all work for calculations and explain reasoning for conceptual questions.

questions.question: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. What is its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground? (Use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Using conservation of energy: PE initial = KE final. PE = mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J, so KE final = 200 J

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: The electromagnetic spectrum ordered by wavelength is: Radio > Microwave > Infrared > Visible > Ultraviolet > X-ray > Gamma ray. Radio waves have the longest wavelength.

questions.question: A 3 kg book is on a 2 m shelf, and a 2 kg book is on a 3 m shelf. Which book has greater gravitational potential energy? (Use g = 10 m/s²)
options: The 3 kg book has greater PE
The 2 kg book has greater PE
Cannot be determined without knowing shelf width
questions.explanation: PE = mgh. For the 3 kg book: PE = 3 × 10 × 2 = 60 J. For the 2 kg book: PE = 2 × 10 × 3 = 60 J. They have equal PE.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave has a frequency of 10¹⁵ Hz. What is its wavelength? (Use c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: Using c = fλ: λ = c/f = (3 × 10⁸)/(10¹⁵) = 3 × 10⁻⁷ m. This is in the ultraviolet region.

questions.question: A person stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is the person from their image?
questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, the image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. Image is 2 m behind mirror, object is 2 m in front, so total distance = 2 + 2 = 4 m.

questions.question: Which statement about kinetic energy is correct?
options: Kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity
Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity
Kinetic energy depends only on mass, not on velocity
Kinetic energy is independent of both mass and velocity
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv², so kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity. Doubling the velocity quadruples the KE.

questions.question: A concave mirror with focal length 10 cm is used. An object is placed 20 cm in front of the mirror. Which describes the image?
questions.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i: 1/10 = 1/20 + 1/d_i, so d_i = 20 cm (positive, real image). Magnification = -d_i/d_o = -20/20 = -1 (inverted, same size). questions.question: In the electromagnetic spectrum, which color of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: The visible spectrum order from longest to shortest wavelength is: Red > Orange > Yellow > Green > Blue > Indigo > Violet. Red has the longest wavelength.

questions.question: True or False: In the absence of friction, total mechanical energy (KE + PE) of a system decreases over time.
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mechanical energy states that in the absence of friction and other non-conservative forces, total mechanical energy remains constant.

questions.question: True or False: Frequency and wavelength of an electromagnetic wave are directly proportional.
questions.explanation: Frequency and wavelength are inversely proportional: as frequency increases, wavelength decreases. Their product equals the speed of light (c = fλ).

questions.question: True or False: A convex mirror can produce a real, inverted, enlarged image.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors always produce virtual, upright, and smaller images. Real, inverted images are produced by concave mirrors when the object is beyond the focal point.

questions.question: A 4 kg object at a height of 5 m has gravitational potential energy of ________ J. (Use g = 10 m/s²)
An electromagnetic wave has a frequency of 3 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Its wavelength is ________ m. (Use c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: λ = c/f = (3 × 10⁸)/(3 × 10¹⁴) = 1 × 10⁻⁶ m or 10⁻⁶ m or 0.000001 m (infrared region)

questions.question: A 5 kg block slides down a frictionless ramp from a height of 8 m. Using conservation of energy, calculate its speed at the bottom of the ramp.
questions.correctAnswer: PE initial = KE final: mgh = ½mv²; v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 8) = √160 ≈ 12.6 m/s

questions.question: Explain why an ultraviolet photon carries more energy than an infrared photon, even though both are electromagnetic waves.
questions.correctAnswer: Energy of an EM wave is E = hf, proportional to frequency. UV has higher frequency than IR, so UV photons carry more energy. Alternatively: UV has shorter wavelength, so higher frequency (c = fλ), resulting in higher energy.
